definition_text: “'Certification' applies to aircraft, engines, or propellers; and, in respect of some certification authorities, auxiliary power units. The certification authorities consider the software as part of the airborne system or equipment installed on the certified product; that is, the certification authorities do not certify the software as a unique, stand-alone product.”
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: Requirements traceability is defined as “the ability to describe and follow the life of a requirement in both a forwards and backwards direction (i.e., from its origins, through its development and specification, to its subsequent deployment and use, and through periods of on-going refinement and iteration in any of these phases).”
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: Avionics is an assembly of electronics subsystems integrated onboard freighter aircraft, military aircraft, business jets, and other private-owned, chartered, and unscheduled aircraft.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: Open systems architecture is a system design approach that aims to produce systems, such as software and hardware, that are inherently interoperable and connectable without recourse to retrofit and redesign.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: The use of a virtual representation or virtual model of a physical system that mimics the functionalities of the actual hardware and software is referred to as a “digital twin.”
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: The process of providing such evidence is known as tool qualification.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: Static code analysis is the analysis of code without actual code execution.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: Code coverage expresses the degree to which the application's source code is exercised by all testing practices, including unit, integration, and system testing—both automated and manual.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: A requirement traceability matrix is an artifact or document that illustrates the linking of requirements with corresponding work items, like a unit test, module source code, architecture design element, other requirements, and so on.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: Instrumented refers to having the user code adorned with additional code to ascertain during execution if that statement, branch, or MC/CD has been executed.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: Service virtualization simulates all of the dependencies needed by the device under test in order to perform full system testing.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf

definition_text: This form of smart test execution is called test impact analysis. It's sometimes referred to as change-based testing.
source_document: KB 2/USA/DO-178C Software Considerations in Airborne Systems.pdf
